desc:
Start with an n × n grid of zeros. Each query is [r1, c1, r2, c2]: add 1 to every cell (r, c) with r1 ≤ r ≤ r2 and c1 ≤ c ≤ c2.

Apply all queries and return the final grid as an array of rows.

n = 3, queries = [[0, 0, 1, 1], [1, 1, 2, 2]]
result = [[1, 1, 0],
          [1, 2, 1],
          [0, 1, 1]]
constraints: 0 ≤ r1 ≤ r2 < n and 0 ≤ c1 ≤ c2 < n
hints: Adding 1 to every cell of every rectangle can cost up to 250,000 operations per query. You need O(1) per query.
In one dimension you mark the start and the cell after the end. In two dimensions a rectangle has four corners to mark.
Do d[r1][c1] += 1, d[r1][c2+1] -= 1, d[r2+1][c1] -= 1, d[r2+1][c2+1] += 1 on an (n+1)×(n+1) grid, then take the 2-D prefix sum: g[r][c] = d[r][c] + g[r-1][c] + g[r][c-1] - g[r-1][c-1].
editorial: The 2-D difference array is the mirror image of the 2-D prefix sum. Marking +1 at the top-left corner, -1 just right of the top-right corner and just below the bottom-left corner, and +1 at the cell diagonally past the bottom-right corner makes the 2-D prefix sum equal 1 exactly inside the rectangle and 0 outside it.

Because the effects are linear, all queries accumulate in the same difference grid. One pass of 2-D prefix sums over the (n+1)×(n+1) grid recovers every cell. Time O(n<sup>2</sup> + q), space O(n<sup>2</sup>). The counts never exceed 100,000.
solution:
def applyRectangles(n, queries):
    d = [[0] * (n + 2) for _ in range(n + 2)]
    for r1, c1, r2, c2 in queries:
        d[r1][c1] += 1
        d[r1][c2 + 1] -= 1
        d[r2 + 1][c1] -= 1
        d[r2 + 1][c2 + 1] += 1
    g = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    out = []
    for r in range(n):
        row = []
        for c in range(n):
            above = g[r - 1][c] if r > 0 else 0
            left = g[r][c - 1] if c > 0 else 0
            diag = g[r - 1][c - 1] if r > 0 and c > 0 else 0
            g[r][c] = d[r][c] + above + left - diag
            row.append(g[r][c])
        out.append(row)
    return out
